message.content:
During the 19th century, one of the most celebrated sculptures was **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (completed in 1889).  
Rodin’s work captured the era’s fascination with realism, emotion, and the human form, and it quickly became emblematic of late‑Victorian artistic innovation.  

While “The Thinker” (first cast in 1902) would later eclipse many works in popular imagination, “The Kiss” remains the quintessential 19th‑century masterpiece that defined the period’s sculptural legacy.
